### The Ultra‑Prolific Thinker

Across the many lists of “greatest minds” in Islamic philosophy, the one that consistently tops the charts—and whose résumé is almost as famous as his name—is **Avicenna (Ibn Sina)**, the Persian polymath who lived from 980‑1037 CE.

| What you’re asking | What the consensus says |
|--------------------|------------------------|
| **Total works credited to Avicenna** | **~450 books** (some counts push it into the mid‑400s). |
| **Works that survived to the present day** | **≈240–260** (floating between 240 + and 260 + depending on the catalogue). |

#### Quick Look at the Numbers

- **Wikipedia** (2023 edits): “He is believed to have written **450 works**; about **240 of them have survived**.”
- **Oxford Dictionary of Islam**: “Some 450 works, of which around 240 survive.”
- **ISOC×**: “The author of approximately **450 works**; a little more than **240 remain in manuscript or early printed editions**.”
- **The British Library** & **University of Oxford** exhibit catalogues that list 236 surviving titles.

> *Note:*  The counting varies because some works are fragments, some are collaborative, and some are later copies in different languages.  In all sources the high‑level figure is “over 400”.

#### A Snapshot of His Output

| Domain | Representative Titles |
|--------|------------------------|
| Philosophy | *The Book of Healing*, *The Canon of Medicine*, *The Book of the Empiricism* |
| Medicine | *The Canon of Medicine* (the world’s most‑used medical textbook of the Middle Ages) |
| Logic | *The Book of the Pen* |
| Metaphysics | *The Dama‘ (Reflection)*, *Discourse on the Receipt of Natural Knowledge* |
| Ethics & Theology | *The Great Book* (Al‑Mawlud), *The Kisāf* (The Fold) |

> These titles alone span the entire spectrum of knowledge that medieval scholarship prized—philosophy, logic, medicine, natural science, and theology.

### Bottom Line

The **most influential philosopher in Islamic history**—**Avicenna (Ibn Sina)**—is credited with **about 450 books**, of which **roughly 240 (or 250+) survive** today. His extraordinary productivity has cemented his place at the top of any ranking of influential Islamic thinkers.
